records.title: Integrated hydrologic model development and postprocessing for GSFLOW using pyGSFLOW
records.description:
pyGSFLOW is a Python package designed to create new GSFLOW integrated hydrologic models, read existing models, edit model input data, run GSFLOW models, process output, and visualize model data.

This archive accompanies the Journal of Open Source Software article "Integrated hydrologic model development and postprocessing for GSFLOW using pyGSFLOW".

Official pyGSFLOW code releases can be found at https://code.usgs.gov/water/pyGSFLOW

records.description: The Danube Delta is a dynamic wetland system where surface and groundwater are closely interconnected, primarily influenced by the water levels of the Danube River. records.title: pyhydra: a modular Python library for hydrological and climate analysis
records.description: pyhydra is a modular Python library for hydrological and climate analysis. It covers the full pipeline from raw data acquisition to stochastic analysis, flood modelling and uncertainty quantification, integrating data sources, extreme value analysis, stochastic generation, HEC-HMS, HEC-RAS and SFINCS automation, and Manning roughness Monte Carlo sensitivity.

records.title: SPHY-MMF - Coupled Hydrology-Hillslope and Channel Erosion Model
records.description: SPHY-MMF is a spatially distributed model that simulates the most relevant hydrological and erosional processes on a cell-by-cell basis and is applied at a daily time step. The model is written in the Python programming language using the PCRaster dynamic modelling framework (https://pcraster.geo.uu.nl/). This version of the model includes a new water routing algorithm, a modification of the sediment transport module and a novel channel morphodynamics module.

records.title: Historical and Projected Hydroclimatic Data for Four European Case Studies
records.description:
This dataset contains historical and projected hydroclimatic data developed within Task 1.1 of the Horizon Europe RECREATE project.

The dataset covers four European case studies: North Holland (Netherlands), Kalundborg (Denmark), Syros (Greece), and Costa Brava (Spain).

The data are derived from CMIP5/EURO-CORDEX climate projections obtained through the Copernicus Climate Data Store. They include a historical reference period (1971–2005) and future projections (2006–2095) under three Representative Concentration Pathway scenarios: RCP2.6, RCP4.5, and RCP8.5.
